entries.creator: Cal Newport
entries.summary:
- Great Restructuring — disruptive technology lowers the value of an individual's labor; employers will increasingly hire machines over people. Further reading: Tyler Cowen's Average Is Over.
- Attention residue — after switching tasks, wor
entries.search:
- Great Restructuring — disruptive technology lowers the value of an individual's labor; employers will increasingly hire machines over people. Further reading: Tyler Cowen's Average Is Over.
- Attention residue — after switching tasks, working memory and attention stay partly on the last one, and performance on the new one drops.
- Distracted high performers — few decision-making roles don't need the quiet of deep work. CEOs are paid for their judgment on solutions, not for producing them.

entries.title: In the Name of Identity: Violence and the Need to Belong
entries.creator: Amin Maalouf
entries.summary: Three parts. First, what identity is: not any single affiliation or piece of heritage, but the combination of all of them that makes a person unique — it can't be divided into halves or thirds. Second, a history of modernization and religio
entries.search:
Three parts. First, what identity is: not any single affiliation or piece of heritage, but the combination of all of them that makes a person unique — it can't be divided into halves or thirds. Second, a history of modernization and religion's role as universal values of human dignity spread; examples of tolerance in both Christianity and Islam; and how tying modernity to the West made non-Western groups feel threatened and cling harder to one facet of identity. Third, how to unite people under modernity while keeping their identities.

Ideas I marked: everyone has a "vertical" heritage from ancestors and community and a "horizontal" one from their contemporaries; we assert our differences so fiercely precisely because we're less and less different; traditions deserve respect only insofar as they respect fundamental human rights.

A poem in class about indigenous people cast aside as irrelevant reminded me of this book: is there a way to keep traditional ways while lifting quality of life? What does progress even mean?

entries.title: Rapt: Attention and the Focused Life
entries.creator: Winifred Gallagher
entries.summary: Personally, I found it quite great. It covered a lot of themes I'd already read, and a few sweeping cultural claims don't hold up — but there's much truth in it. It doesn't claim meditation is the answer; it argues that attention lies at th
entries.search:
Personally, I found it quite great. It covered a lot of themes I'd already read, and a few sweeping cultural claims don't hold up — but there's much truth in it. It doesn't claim meditation is the answer; it argues that attention lies at the core of our existence.

The most interesting part: research on flow, and how early-childhood experiences set up the capacity for difficult work that makes later concentration and flow possible. Analyzing that across cultures could be fruitful.

A possible meditation target: two spheres of attention, top-down and bottom-up. We can set our objects of awareness — whether we attend to the positive or the negative is up to us.

entries.title: Attention Restoration Theory
entries.summary: An approach to restoring attention. Environments with stimuli that modestly engage involuntary attention let directed attention recover.
entries.search:
An approach to restoring attention. Environments with stimuli that modestly engage involuntary attention let directed attention recover.

Attention splits into bottom-up (involuntary) and top-down (voluntary). Directed attention is the part of top-down attention that has to suppress distracting stimulation — and it's the part that tires.

The study (The Cognitive Benefits of Interacting with Nature): people walked for an hour in either an urban or a natural setting. The nature walkers did better on the backward digit-span test and on an Attention Network Task, and their mood improved (though mood wasn't what explained the attention gains).

- Backward digit span — listen to sequences of 3–9 digits, repeat them backwards. Measures directed-attention performance.
- PANAS (Positive and Negative Affect Schedule) — rate mood adjectives 1–5 for how well they describe you right now.

I moved seats once just to stop looking at dirt — actively implementing this. I wonder whether it actually changes performance on attention tasks.

entries.title: Constraint relaxation
entries.summary: Some problems are effectively intractable — they're solved in O(n!) time, so the truly optimal answer can't be reached in a tractable amount of time. Relax the constraints and you reach a semi-optimal solution in a fraction of the time.
entries.search:
Some problems are effectively intractable — they're solved in O(n!) time, so the truly optimal answer can't be reached in a tractable amount of time. Relax the constraints and you reach a semi-optimal solution in a fraction of the time.

Its cousin is overfitting: certain data values get over-prioritized, and the model stops generalizing beyond the data set it was built on.

Both carry over to human decisions. I can overfit a decision — too many variables, too many what-ifs. Relaxing the constraints cuts through it. The question that does this: what job would you pick if you won the lottery? It lets me look past the variables that distract from the intention behind the choice, and decide with less effort and less excessive weighing of every factor.

entries.title: Darwin's idea
entries.summary: Natural selection: organisms vary, the variants that suit the needs of their environment are selected for, and the population changes.
entries.search:
Natural selection: organisms vary, the variants that suit the needs of their environment are selected for, and the population changes.

When Darwin proposed it, the unit of heredity — the gene — hadn't been identified. Mendel's work would come out years later and take much longer to reach mainstream science. Groundbreaking as the idea was, it took a lot of further work to show it was right and displace the paradigms of the time.

See Galapagos Finch, and the idea it displaced: Law of Use and Disuse.

entries.title: Emic and etic
entries.summary: Two perspectives on a culture, named after phonetic vs phonemic:
entries.search:
Two perspectives on a culture, named after phonetic vs phonemic:

- Etic (from phonetic — the sounds) — the outsider's objective evaluation of a culture's activities or customs.
- Emic (from phonemic — the meaning) — the insider's perspective on what those activities and conditions mean.

A related point from the same class: we all have the capacity for the same primary emotions across cultures, but how they're interpreted and understood depends on the cultural context we live in.

entries.title: Four social theories of global health
entries.summary: From a medical anthropology class in Seville. Medical anthropology studies health, healing, and illness within their political, economic, and social context.
entries.search:
From a medical anthropology class in Seville. Medical anthropology studies health, healing, and illness within their political, economic, and social context.

1. Unintended consequences of social action. Institutions trying to do good cause later harm. Forced vaccination campaigns bred vaccine hesitancy that undermined later public-health efforts.
2. Social suffering.
   - Health systems can do harm — medical error, waiting times, misdiagnosis, poorly informed treatment.
   - Social causes produce health problems — poverty, high-stress environments, food deserts, no sanitation or clean water, toxic exposure.
   - Social and health problems are hard to separate: is someone ill because of a disease, or the chronic stress of living in poverty? Social policy and health policy are often one and the same.
   - The individual isn't the only sufferer. A person with Alzheimer's has a family watching them lose their memory; disease ripples through social networks.
3. Social construction of reality. What health is, what counts as acceptable treatment and healthy behavior — all depend on the cultural reality people live in.
4. Biopower. Governments and corporations shape how our biology manifests — which products they offer, which choices they allow, which body types get manufactured consent.

entries.title: Galapagos finch
entries.summary: One of the observations that led Darwin to natural selection: 14 finch species on the Galapagos whose main difference was the beak, each one suited to how that species fed.
entries.search:
One of the observations that led Darwin to natural selection: 14 finch species on the Galapagos whose main difference was the beak, each one suited to how that species fed.

They share a single common ancestor, so the differences really are adaptations. Field work has since watched selection happen in these populations: in years of heavy rain or drought, different food sources become common, and the species (and individuals) that can reach them thrive.

The same work shows how the birds keep species apart — visual cues (beak, appearance) and song — which prevents cross-species breeding that would otherwise homogenize the gene pool.

entries.title: Group selection vs individual selection
entries.summary: Groups are a collection of individuals each acting to optimize their own well-being. That includes supposed altruism — we're altruistic when there's a benefit likely to pay off over time.
entries.search:
Groups are a collection of individuals each acting to optimize their own well-being. That includes supposed altruism — we're altruistic when there's a benefit likely to pay off over time.

Assuming a group will be inherently altruistic ignores drift and mutation. In the real world a selfish mutant would be advantaged and spread, exploiting everyone else's altruism.

- Signaling theory. Even acts with no possible payback signal to the community who is trustworthy and generous.
- Tit for tat. Further reading: The Selfish Gene.

entries.title: Law of use and disuse
entries.summary: Crystallized by Jean-Baptiste Lamarck: changes in an animal's morphology from use (or disuse) accumulate and lead to differences between species.
entries.search:
Crystallized by Jean-Baptiste Lamarck: changes in an animal's morphology from use (or disuse) accumulate and lead to differences between species.

Wrong, but significant — it questioned the permanence of species, whether they could change at all.

entries.title: Limbic friction
entries.summary: The resistance you feel when you know there's something you can do and you're refusing to do it — the friction my brain generates whenever I want to start an activity.
entries.search:
The resistance you feel when you know there's something you can do and you're refusing to do it — the friction my brain generates whenever I want to start an activity.

One way through it: make a list of painful activities and make yourself do them. Steepen and deepen the trough of amotivation and pain:
- cold shower or ice bath
- a meditation session
- a set number of pushups, squats, situps
- learning something difficult

entries.title: Mendel's law of independent assortment
entries.summary: The law: inheriting one allele doesn't affect inheriting another.
entries.search:
The law: inheriting one allele doesn't affect inheriting another.

In reality, false. Alleles can be linked — having one makes you more likely to have the other — because of where they sit on the chromosome. Genes close together tend to stay together through recombination. The distance is measured in centimorgans.

That exception is useful: linkage helps locate genes. Once a gene's location is mapped, genetic testing becomes possible, and its protein product can be studied toward a therapeutic.

Two single-gene examples of Mendel's first law:
- Huntington disease — dominant; 50% of an affected parent's children inherit it. Starts in middle adulthood with personality changes, forgetfulness, involuntary movements; ends in loss of motor control and intellect.
- Phenylketonuria — recessive; the enzyme that processes phenylalanine doesn't work, causing cognitive deficits. Found when blood tests showed high phenylalanine in people with intellectual disability.

entries.title: Modality effect
entries.summary: How the mode of presenting material affects memory and learning.
entries.search:
How the mode of presenting material affects memory and learning.

For serial recall, auditory beats visual (4.8 vs 5.36 words).

This relationship is interesting. Words are first taken in as visual images and then translated into their language components, so it would follow that presenting language-based material by ear is more efficient. There might also be something in how information enters working memory — whether running two modalities at once uses cognitive resources more efficiently.

entries.title: Morbidity risk estimate
entries.summary: The chance of being affected by a disorder over an entire lifetime, age-corrected — because the risk of getting a disease often depends on age. Schizophrenia, for example, doesn't show until late adolescence or later.
entries.search:
The chance of being affected by a disorder over an entire lifetime, age-corrected — because the risk of getting a disease often depends on age. Schizophrenia, for example, doesn't show until late adolescence or later.

Schizophrenia lifetime risk by relation to someone affected: second-degree relative 4%, first-degree 9%, fraternal twin 17%, identical twin 48%.

entries.title: Positive and negative life experiences
entries.summary: Positive life experiences cluster in young adulthood (20–45), with the adoption of more social roles — living alone, a job, new friends, partners, other responsibilities. Over that period, neuroticism goes down.
entries.search:
Positive life experiences cluster in young adulthood (20–45), with the adoption of more social roles — living alone, a job, new friends, partners, other responsibilities. Over that period, neuroticism goes down.

How are we defining a positive life experience, though, and why would taking on more roles reduce neuroticism? Is autonomy the driving factor in the growth of the individual? What else could explain it?

Negative life experiences are spread more evenly across the lifespan — they're deviations from life's normal progress — though they still trend upward over time.

entries.title: Present orientation
entries.summary: Being in the present avoids the short-circuiting of self-conscious thought. Self-conscious thoughts turn into rumination, and attention gets fed into them, taking resources from problem-solving. Like thinking about whether you'll make the s
entries.search:
Being in the present avoids the short-circuiting of self-conscious thought. Self-conscious thoughts turn into rumination, and attention gets fed into them, taking resources from problem-solving. Like thinking about whether you'll make the shot while you're shooting — it takes you out of flow.

That's why spontaneous speaking is hard: the self-conscious circuits switch on.

Ways to cultivate it:
- Reframe challenging questions as the biggest opportunities. Someone challenging you is engaged — they want to understand.
- Shoot for average, fail cheerfully.
- Be obvious; that's where your truest voice is.
- Be uncomfortable enough to plug in — get lost on purpose and see what you find.

entries.title: Principal component analysis
entries.summary: A dimensionality-reduction method: re-express many variables as a smaller set of uncorrelated linear combinations of them.
entries.search:
A dimensionality-reduction method: re-express many variables as a smaller set of uncorrelated linear combinations of them.

The steps:
- Fit a line of best fit through the data. The vector along it is an eigenvector; the proportions of each variable in it are the loading scores.
- The eigenvectors and eigenvalues come from the covariance matrix — variances on the diagonal, covariances off it.
- An eigenvalue is the variance captured by that component. All eigenvalues sum to the total variance of the original variables, so each one's share is the percentage of variation it explains.
- Project the data onto the eigenvectors with the largest eigenvalues. A scree plot shows the variation per component; a common cutoff is eigenvalue  1.

Things to remember:
- You can have as many components as original variables.
- PCA does nothing if the original variables aren't correlated.
- Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin tests whether variables are factorable: overall  0.5, individual  0.8.

entries.title: Progression of language
entries.summary: The move from pictorial to phonetic alphabets changed our mental capacities.
entries.search:
The move from pictorial to phonetic alphabets changed our mental capacities.

Sumerian cuneiform and Egyptian hieroglyphs were logosyllabic: the reader first had to analyze a character to work out how it was being used. That took more processing, and made literacy slow to learn and slow to spread.

The Greeks' phonetic alphabet created an economy of characters — less time and attention to recognize symbols, fewer cognitive resources. Brain studies comparing readers of phonetic and pictorial scripts back this up.

The cost of abstraction: McLuhan thought preliterate people had a more "sensuous" involvement with the world. Literacy and the analytical thinking it brings let us abstract away from lived experience — and detach from feeling.

entries.title: Self-talk ritual
entries.summary: From Mark Queppet's The Reboot Regimen. The point: improve the quality of internal discussion so the rational mind can interpret emotional responses and steer them toward actions that help.
entries.search:
From Mark Queppet's The Reboot Regimen. The point: improve the quality of internal discussion so the rational mind can interpret emotional responses and steer them toward actions that help.

1. Ground. Tension in the body tracks negative emotion and short-circuits relaxed, rational thinking. A few deep breaths, a body scan, engage the senses.
2. Connect. Bring awareness to the emotional center and observe whatever's there, without judgment. You can't change what's there, only notice it.
3. Translate. Put the felt sense into a sentence. Don't filter — we think a lot of nonsense; we aren't meant to take every thought seriously.
4. Respond — with truth, as a friend, as a leader. Accept the desire, then state honestly what acting on it leads to, and whether it moves you toward your best life.

You have to feed these truths to yourself in the moment.

entries.title: Split-attention effect
entries.summary: Extraneous cognitive load caused by how information is presented and organized. The classic case: a geometry diagram with the information you need to solve for its sides and angles printed separately, so you keep looking back and forth betw
entries.search: Extraneous cognitive load caused by how information is presented and organized. The classic case: a geometry diagram with the information you need to solve for its sides and angles printed separately, so you keep looking back and forth between the two.

entries.title: The map is not the territory
entries.summary: A map of reality isn't reality — maps are imperfect.
entries.search:
A map of reality isn't reality — maps are imperfect.

We need abstractions: descriptions, theories, models. But every map has three problems:
- It can be incorrect without our realizing it.
- It's a reduction of the real thing, so it loses fidelity.
- It needs interpretation, which can introduce major errors.

entries.title: The voice inside your head
entries.summary: The voice in our head is constantly trying to find a comfortable resting place — internal coherence, the brain's need to fit new information into its existing schemas. It will change viewpoints and shift perspective to get there. It reminds
entries.search:
The voice in our head is constantly trying to find a comfortable resting place — internal coherence, the brain's need to fit new information into its existing schemas. It will change viewpoints and shift perspective to get there. It reminds me of the hedonic treadmill: this voice keeps moving the set-point for silence.

Is the voice me? No — I'm the one observing it. Put three objects in front of you and ask which one you are; none of them, you're the one looking. Same for the inner voice.

The commotion the mind makes about life is the real problem. Thinking about how things should change, or disliking how they are, does nothing to change them.

Why do we narrate? Labeling what we observe makes us feel we have a relationship with it — it's been seen, labeled, judged, run through our values and history. There's always some thought that makes the experience feel controlled: noticing it's cold, then comforting yourself that you'll be home in a few minutes. What about that thought was necessary?

entries.title: Time-keeping
entries.summary: The clock made "the abstract framework of divided time" the point of reference for thought and action — and with it, belief in a world of mathematically measurable sequences.
entries.search:
The clock made "the abstract framework of divided time" the point of reference for thought and action — and with it, belief in a world of mathematically measurable sequences.

- For most of history, time was a continuous, cyclical flow, set by agrarian rhythms. Things just took as long as they took; there was no way to measure whether something was done "better."
- Personal timekeeping put every individual in control of their own time — possibly a stimulus to Western individualism.

This connects to Four Thousand Weeks. I agree that mechanizing time made room for productivity to be a topic at all. Once you can measure how long something takes, you can show objectively whether it's "efficient" — and the pressure to be efficient follows.

entries.title: A relentless focus on quality beats speed
entries.summary: I've been reaching for quick, easier solutions in the name of progress and efficiency — partly because I feel the need to finish faster and be more productive.
entries.search:
I've been reaching for quick, easier solutions in the name of progress and efficiency — partly because I feel the need to finish faster and be more productive.

With a relentless focus on quality, I make fewer mistakes, which limits the extra work I have to do in the first place, and the work itself is higher quality and higher impact. The interesting projects in front of me need the time and energy, plus that focus on quality, to develop the expertise they call for.

entries.title: Brains built for tribes are mismatched with modern technology
entries.summary: There's a significant problem in how our brains — shaped first for Paleolithic life, then for Neolithic life in small tribes, and later for organizing around cultural myths into larger social structures — interact with the technology we're
entries.search:
There's a significant problem in how our brains — shaped first for Paleolithic life, then for Neolithic life in small tribes, and later for organizing around cultural myths into larger social structures — interact with the technology we're exposed to now.

The modes of thinking cultivated by those older ways of living collide with modern tech, causing tension, conflict, and misaligned aims and incentives.

entries.title: Clear writing comes from clear thinking
entries.summary: Reading back my own writing, I fail to be concise and add filler. Even some of the "ands" are just a wish to be verbose. State what I feel, without adding justifications and reasons for it.
entries.search:
Reading back my own writing, I fail to be concise and add filler. Even some of the "ands" are just a wish to be verbose. State what I feel, without adding justifications and reasons for it.

To what extent have I prioritized complex sentences over clear ideas? Cut the unnecessary, verbose phrasing into authoritative, direct statements. Hard-to-read writing frustrates readers; it's only accessible to people who already believe you have something to say, never to someone coming to your words for the first time.

Clarity in writing comes from clarity in thought — the two are inextricably linked. Avoiding that work lands you in pseudo-intellectual territory: knowledge and phrases that carry depth only at first glance.

Being a writer isn't just having ideas; it's writing about them well — using the full extent of the language while minimizing complexity. Getting words onto the page is easy for me now. Going back over them and conveying them clearly still escapes me. (On Writing Well helped: much of what passes for grammar is really style.)

entries.title: Give the morning's best hours to deep work
entries.summary: Set up the morning to use its 3–4 hours of concentration, and let the rest of the day be carried by the wind and the remaining tasks.
entries.search:
Set up the morning to use its 3–4 hours of concentration, and let the rest of the day be carried by the wind and the remaining tasks.

Much better than cramming work that needs serious focus into short gaps where I can't focus deeply on it anyway. See Deep Work on attention residue.

entries.title: Grades and competition crowd out intrinsic motivation
entries.summary: Competition and grading are external motivators, and they reduce the drive that's intrinsic. When an early sense of security, autonomy, social support, and ability is threatened and made contingent on external rewards, a person has to work
entries.search:
Competition and grading are external motivators, and they reduce the drive that's intrinsic. When an early sense of security, autonomy, social support, and ability is threatened and made contingent on external rewards, a person has to work against their intrinsically motivating forces.

My ideal state is being entirely intrinsically motivated, while still having the markers of success in the society we live in.

Someone had to design the learning systems we're put through; they don't arise naturally. Would I have been taught how to naturally retain and remember, or would it always have been a struggle? And in my own classes I find it frankly ridiculous that we're told to learn in these ways instead of by ourselves — online, or reading to learn.

entries.title: Group conversation reverts to the mean
entries.summary: An individual is a crowd, and a crowd is an individual. That's how talking with groups feels: the reversion to the mean. The conversation can't escape or change topic except to jump to the most identifiable idea, rather than the deepest tho
entries.search: An individual is a crowd, and a crowd is an individual. That's how talking with groups feels: the reversion to the mean. The conversation can't escape or change topic except to jump to the most identifiable idea, rather than the deepest thought or insight we could try to inspire in each other.

entries.title: Hurry leaves no room for depth
entries.summary: I hurry through life. I want things done fast, I want "better" ways of doing things — and I often can't find the patience and calm to hear a friend out, which is the truest display of empathy.
entries.search:
I hurry through life. I want things done fast, I want "better" ways of doing things — and I often can't find the patience and calm to hear a friend out, which is the truest display of empathy.

What's the belief underneath? Anything that wants the world to unfold in a way it doesn't. Hurry, at the core. There's no room for reflection during hurry. No room for kindness. No room for deep thought — hurry is the antithesis of deep. We can't keep a sense of calm and patience and understanding while constantly in the throes of hurry.

entries.title: Name overwhelm early or it becomes burnout
entries.summary: Being able to identify the feeling of being overwhelmed is crucial to managing workload. Failing to notice it is a recipe for burnout.
entries.search: Being able to identify the feeling of being overwhelmed is crucial to managing workload. Failing to notice it is a recipe for burnout.

entries.title: People pay far less attention to you than you think
entries.summary: People really don't care what you're doing nearly as much as you think. They're paying attention to their own lives, their own realities, what's going on with them.
entries.search:
People really don't care what you're doing nearly as much as you think. They're paying attention to their own lives, their own realities, what's going on with them.

Sitting and observing a conversation without a goal: the words matter less than you'd think. Tonality carries much of the meaning in human conversation.

entries.title: Reading without review mostly evaporates
entries.summary: There's no purpose to reading educational material without making review material for it. Otherwise I won't make progress in my understanding.
entries.search:
There's no purpose to reading educational material without making review material for it. Otherwise I won't make progress in my understanding.

My retention of a text depends on how long it's been since I last read it and how many days in a row I read and reviewed it — spaced repetition and consistency, plainly. Writing and speaking about what I learned, then reviewing and speaking about it again, would help too.

What the review material should look like:
1. Cards I can review in a year and still know what source they came from and what concept they mean.
2. Atomic — the smallest possible unit. The organization comes from integrating those atoms into my own schema.

Two years later in medical school, same lesson from Anki: information under regular spaced repetition is closer at hand than anything recalled after long gaps.

entries.title: Self-referential thoughts should earn their keep
entries.summary: Every self-referential thought should go under the magnifying glass: is it contributing to action toward my goals?
entries.search:
Every self-referential thought should go under the magnifying glass: is it contributing to action toward my goals?

What good does thinking I'm unintelligent do? It makes me shirk and stop taking in information, believing I can't understand it.

entries.title: Shared presence is enough for friendship
entries.summary: Social interactions don't need to signal complete understanding, reach a shared understanding of a topic, or even touch our baseline emotions. They can be as simple as shared presence — someone in the room, a repeated interaction, a warm wa
entries.search:
Social interactions don't need to signal complete understanding, reach a shared understanding of a topic, or even touch our baseline emotions. They can be as simple as shared presence — someone in the room, a repeated interaction, a warm wave from a regular you see.

Those are the interactions that activate the prosocial networks of the brain and the positive response that comes with them. In what way am I failing to take advantage of them?

entries.title: The words I know limit the thoughts I can think
entries.summary: Learning Spanish: it's hard to transfer how I think into the language. Thoughts flow differently, bounded by the words I know. I think less politically and less complexly, because the words don't come quickly. In English I can convey though
entries.search:
Learning Spanish: it's hard to transfer how I think into the language. Thoughts flow differently, bounded by the words I know. I think less politically and less complexly, because the words don't come quickly. In English I can convey thoughts with subtlety — or, put another way, be wordy. In Spanish there's no room for long, drawn-out sentences; I have to finish forming the thought first.

The other direction is true too: people who know different languages live a different experience of the world. Different words for facets of nature and environment make reality richer and more detailed.

And words have a cost. They might reduce our capacity to experience the world directly — pulling us outside the body, sorting things into categories. What I can experience in any state of mind isn't fully expressible in words; it's the difference between labeling an experience and not labeling it.

On learning vocabulary: mapping a Spanish word back to English is three layers of processing (thing → English → Spanish) instead of two. Better to tie the word directly to an image, idea, or felt sensation.

entries.title: When I feel purposeless or anxious, I should work out
entries.summary: After vigorous cardio I feel much more comfortable in my own mind — not racing, grounded and stable.
entries.search:
After vigorous cardio I feel much more comfortable in my own mind — not racing, grounded and stable.

The axiom to remember: whenever I feel depressed, purposeless, or anxious, work out. Run, walk, get the heart rate up, bring the body to physical exhaustion. Once I'm no longer brimming with energy for the myriad ideas my mind throws at me, I can be selective and pick the ones worth pursuing.
